previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, COPD, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for acute on chronic systolic heart failure and recurrent syncope associated with coughing. He presented with significant weight gain (89.8 kg from a dry weight of 82 kg), orthopnea, and multiple episodes of cough-induced syncope, sometimes with urinary incontinence. He was treated with IV furosemide and metolazone, achieving diuresis and a discharge weight of 82.2 kg. His cough improved with optimized GERD treatment, azithromycin for COPD, and symptomatic management. No arrhythmias were detected on telemetry, and syncope did not recur during admission. Cocaine was detected in his urine, which limited beta-blocker initiation. He was discharged home on increased torsemide, continued metolazone, and uptitrated insulin, with plans for cardiology follow-up and a repeat CT for a known right upper lobe nodule.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure

and over stimulation in the setting of severe CM, especially 
with reports of low SBP initially by EMS/ED. There have been
